1. (S) SITUATION:
Soviet support shipping and staging facilities beyond the eastern choke points are sustaining raider operations against coalition sea lanes. RAAF F-111Cs from Learmonth will conduct a detached long-range strike against the marked convoy before withdrawing to base.
2. (S) MISSION: 2.1 Destroy the target anchorage. 2.2 At least one F-111C must survive.
3. (S) EXECUTION: 3.1 Depart Learmonth and follow the marked strike axis using the assigned navigation plan. 3.2 Confirm the target convoy before weapons release and concentrate attacks on support shipping and staging facilities. 3.3 Use stand-off weapons where possible and avoid protracted operations over the target area. 3.4 Egress immediately after the strike and recover at Learmonth. Do not wait for a second attack window.
4. (S) ENEMY SITUATION: 4.1 Soviet auxiliaries and support vessels are concentrated at the target anchorage. 4.2 Local air or surface units may respond after the first weapons impact. 4.3 The enemy may have only limited warning, but recovery forces can reach the area if the strike is delayed.
5. (S) FRIENDLY SITUATION: 5.1 RAAF F-111C aircraft form the primary strike package. 5.2 Learmonth is the designated recovery base and remains outside the immediate target area.
6. (S) INTEL ASSESSMENT: 6.1 Dry-season conditions favor long-range navigation and strike operations, although high cloud or haze may complicate visual target confirmation. 6.2 Destruction of the convoy will disrupt the enemy's ability to sustain operations around Sunda and Lombok. 6.3 Aircraft survival is mandatory. Abort secondary targets if the primary strike is complete and the package is threatened.
